name: John Farnham
description:
'''John Peter Farnham''' (born 1 July 1949), is a British-born Australian singer, actor, and television personality. As '''Johnny Farnham''', he was a [[Teen idol|teen pop idol]] from 1967 to 1979 and thereafter was an [[Adult contemporary music|adult contemporary]] entertainer, becoming one of Australia's best-known and most popular performers and the only Australian musical artist to have a number-one single or album in each of six consecutive decades. He was [[talent manager|managed]] by [[Darryl Sambell]] from 1967 to 1976 and by his long-term friend [[Glenn Wheatley]] from 1980 until Wheatley's death in 2022. Farnham married former dancer Jillian Billman in 1973 and the couple have two children.

Farnham's first commercially successful recording was the American-written [[novelty song]] "[[Sadie (The Cleaning Lady)]]". Released in November 1967 the song gave Farnham widespread recognition in Australia. He subsequently replaced [[Glenn Shorrock]] as lead singer of [[Little River Band]] (LRB) from 1982 to 1986 but otherwise has worked mostly as a solo artist. In November 1986 his solo single "[[You're the Voice]]" peaked at No. 1 on the [[Kent Music Report|Australian singles charts]], and the associated album, ''[[Whispering Jack]]'', held the number-one position on the album charts for a total of 25 weeks. ''Whispering Jack'' is the [[List of best-selling albums in Australia|third-highest-selling album in Australian history]] and {{as of|September 2026|lc=yes}} remains the highest-selling album in Australia by any Australian artist. Both the single and the album also had international success, with the album reaching No. 6 in the United Kingdom and No. 1 in Sweden. Farnham's other number-one recordings are the singles "[[Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head]]" (1970) and "[[Age of Reason (song)|Age of Reason]]" (1988), and the albums ''[[Age of Reason (album)|Age of Reason]]'' (1988), ''[[Chain Reaction (John Farnham album)|Chain Reaction]]'' (1990), ''[[Then Again (John Farnham album)|Then Again...]]'' (1993), ''[[33⅓ (album)|33⅓]]'' (2000), ''[[The Last Time (album)|The Last Time]]'' (2002), and ''[[Two Strong Hearts Live]]'' (2015). He has toured with numerous artists including [[the Seekers]], [[Stevie Nicks]], and [[Lionel Richie]], and has released three collaborative albums with [[Olivia Newton-John]] and one with [[Tom Jones (singer)|Tom Jones]].

Farnham has been recognised with [[List of awards and nominations received by John Farnham|numerous honours and awards]], including [[Australian of the Year]] (1987), [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] (1996), 22 [[ARIA Music Awards]] (including his 2003 induction into the [[ARIA Hall of Fame]]), and he was voted '[[Australian pop music awards#1967–1978: King of Pop Awards|King of Pop]]' by ''[[TV Week]]'' magazine readers for five consecutive years from 1969 to 1973. Aside from his recording career Farnham has acted in musical theatre with lead roles in Australian productions of ''[[Charlie Girl]]'' (1971), ''[[Pippin (musical)|Pippin]]'' (1974), and ''[[Jesus Christ Superstar]]'' (1992). He starred in his own TV series and specials, including ''It's Magic'' (with [[Colleen Hewett]], 1974), ''[[Bobby Dazzler]]'' (1977–78), and ''Farnham and Byrne'' (with [[Debra Byrne]], 1980), as well as appearing as a guest on numerous  television shows, including ''[[The Don Lane Show]]'', ''[[Countdown (Australian TV series)|Countdown]]'', and ''[[Hey Hey It's Saturday]]''.

Farnham has not performed publicly since February 2020. In August 2022 a cancerous tumour was successfully removed from his mouth in an operation involving jaw reconstruction. His autobiography ''The Voice Inside'' (2024), was co-written with Poppy Stockell. In May 2026 Farnham announced that, "because of the surgeries to my mouth and face over the past few years, singing on stage is not something I can consider again". On 20 September 2026 numerous local and international artists presented a tribute concert, ''The Songs of John Farnham: A Living Legend''. However, Farnham was unable to attend due to his poor health.
